criteria.rationale: D1 rests on the levels being ordered (review_plan.go ranks same-actor-separate-execution 1, different-actor 2, mandatory-human 3) and on the declared path, which already accepts any agent: or human: reviewer at this level (review_closeout.go). The abm R5 wording is ambiguous; the ordering reading is the consistent one and D1 records it.
Pure synchronous validation in verifiedAuthorityBlockers; no shared state, goroutines or lifecycle change.

Attestation, claim and policy schemas unchanged; only one blocker message disappears. different-actor and mandatory-human branches are untouched; TestABMReviewAuthorityRejectsSameActor and RejectsSameExecution still pass.
A claim missing implementation principal or execution is still refused at this level; same review and implementation execution is still refused whoever reviews (R2), covered by the ownRun case.

Only verified-assurance instances requiring same-actor-separate-execution are affected, and only by accepting more separated reviews; declared assurance behaviour is unchanged. Harne8 needs a pin containing dd4b47d3, as the spec states.
Remaining blockers still name the missing fields or the shared execution; no secrets or key material are printed.
Relaxation only: every attestation that verified before still verifies; no CLI flag, schema or policy value changes.

Reviewed the full diff of dd4b47d3 (the only commit with the trailer). The removed branch was the only same-principal requirement; the separate-execution check remains. The new test fails on the parent code with the exact refusal and passes on HEAD. pose validate --tolerant --json-out .pose/results/delivery-validation.json at 59aab417: 130/131 checks pass; the single failure is pose-mcp/go/test, only in TestUpdateDryRunListsWhatTheUpdateChanges (spec pose-update-dry-run-reports-the-whole-update, not this spec): the action request id includes RequestedAt truncated to the second, so the dry-run and the real update name different act-* files when they straddle a second boundary. Reproduced on b4e9e81a, the commit before this spec (1 of 300 runs of go test -count=300), so the failure predates this change; internal/pose, the only package this spec touches, passed in the same run. The spec test TestSameActorLevelAdmitsADifferentActor was also run directly: passes on HEAD and fails on dd4b47d3 with review_bundle.go reverted, with the refusal Harne8 met.
Root cause is the equality-of-principals branch contradicting the ordering comment directly above it; the fix removes that branch. assess design observed 4/4 files with no structural deltas.

Applied review workflow, security and documentation-style rules. The code comment, spec D1 and changelog fragment explain the change; no manual describes same-actor-separate-execution as requiring the same principal, so no doc update is owed.
Removes a refusal operators could not work around except by lowering separation; no new configuration.

R1: the other case in TestSameActorLevelAdmitsADifferentActor verifies with no blockers. R2: the ownRun case is refused with separate execution. Also covered: same actor in a separate run still accepted.

artifact-check: 5 claims, 5 observed, single commit dd4b47d3. Only this spec is being closed; no code, policy or capabilities changed by the review. Reviewer identity: the prefix agent:independent- is a declaration required by the engine; this review is another execution of the same vendor and model as the implementer (Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5, agent:claude-opus-5-5), done as fallback because the other-vendor reviewer (Codex) was unavailable: independence of execution, not of vendor, authorised by the maintainer.

Weakening check reviewed adversarially: an implementer cannot self-approve under this level by naming another principal, because the claim is signed by a trusted issuer and the execution must still differ; at this level the declared path already admits any agent. Higher levels keep principal inequality and human role checks. No secrets in the diff.
Deleting two lines and adding one test is the smallest correct change; no new mode or flag.
